title: Machine-learning-guided screening validates 14 previously unreported drug–GPCR interactions
summary: Chemical Space Neural Networks used network-neighborhood labels to predict drug–target interactions and were evaluated with a yeast biosensor screen of 3,773 compound–GPCR pairs (539 compounds and seven human GPCRs). The authors report 14 experimentally significant interactions with no prior literature/database evidence in the relevant chemical neighborhoods, tentatively linking some to adverse effects. This is an in-vitro receptor-screen discovery, not clinical proof of drug side effects.
ai_technology: Chemical Space Neural Networks (CSNN), neighborhood-to-prediction model using network homophily and graph neural networks with labels as features
organization: Technical University of Denmark; Biomia ApS; Joint BioEnergy Institute; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; University of California, Berkeley

evidence.tested: The authors report 14 experimentally significant interactions with no prior literature/database evidence in the relevant chemical neighborhoods, tentatively linking some to adverse effects.
evidence.unknown: Yeast assay is a heterologous in-vitro system and does not establish physiological effects in humans. The article describes the 14 interactions as potentially linked to adverse effects, not confirmed clinical adverse events. Some assay limitations and false positives are discussed; precision for predicted positives is limited.
evidence.ai_role: Used chemical-neighborhood labels to prioritize/annotate compound–GPCR interactions; model outputs were compared with high-throughput yeast biosensor measurements to identify previously unreported hits.
